mainEntity.name: How can I tell if past owners already did a seismic retrofit on my Los Angeles property?

acceptedAnswer.text:
To check for prior seismic retrofitting, you’ll need to combine document research with a physical inspection. Many upgrades are hidden behind finishes but leave a paper and permit trail.

Start with city building records for permits mentioning seismic, structural, foundation, or soft‑story work. Then have a structural engineer or experienced contractor walk the property to look for typical retrofit elements.

Key factors:
- City or county permit history, including final inspections
- Presence of foundation anchor bolts, shear panels, steel frames, and new concrete
- Engineer’s letters, old retrofit contracts, or inspection reports from prior owners
- Any visible reinforcement at garages, carports, or cripple walls

Ask the seller for all construction records and make seismic review part of your due diligence. If evidence is unclear, budget for at least partial upgrades.

A knowledgeable inspector can often recognize retrofit work, but documentation is what future buyers and lenders will care about most.
